findings.title: Authentication model stays aligned with the HLD
findings.description: The HLD (`100-arch.orchestration-v2.md`, Authentication Patterns) states squadron does not unify authentication and each provider's credential resolution is self-contained. The design argues this correctly: `InteractiveLogin` is an optional capability implemented only by `OAuthFileStrategy`, the `AuthStrategy` Protocol is unchanged, credentials stay exclusively in `~/.codex/auth.json`, and login/logout/account delegate to the Codex runtime. No squadron-side token store is added (Excluded, line 42), so no shared auth layer is introduced. The rationale for deferring an HLD edit until a second provider adopts the capability is proportionate.

findings.title: Provider boundaries and dependency direction match slice 128
findings.description: `openai_codex` is imported only inside functions; SDK types are confined to `agent.py` and `login.py`; `runtime.py` probes importability only. The provider still registers without the extra, so the review pipeline (which slice 128 moved onto `Agent.handle_message()` via the registry) is untouched, and the core engine gains no provider-internal dependency. D3 (line 99) and D9 (line 112) use capability `isinstance` checks rather than the profile-name/auth-type string dispatch slice 128 banned, and Technical Requirements (line 198) pins that as a criterion. `interfaces: []` in frontmatter is honest about there being no downstream consumer, and `parent:` correctly names the slice plan.

findings.title: Upstream integration contracts are consumed as provided
findings.description: The design names the exact interfaces slice 931 provides (`AgentConfig.effort`, `ProviderCapabilities.applies_effort`, `core/usage.py` `TokenUsage`/`RunTelemetry`) and the message-metadata keys the OpenAI agent already stamps (`metadata["usage"]`, `["turns"]`), so D5/D6 close #171 and add usage without changing review artifacts or `review/` imports. Slice 128's registry, capabilities and `"oauth"` auth type are listed as prerequisites (line 49). `applies_effort=True` plus dropping the 931 WARNING is the correct counterpart to 931 D4. The 128/931 prerequisites are both marked complete in their own designs.

findings.title: Turn-path failure modes are enumerated with explicit handling
findings.description: The 14-row table gives a concrete strategy for hang (`asyncio.timeout(codex.turn_timeout_s)` + cancel), peer disconnect mid-turn (`TransportClosedError` → `ProviderError`, client state reset), startup/initialize failure, server busy/rate limit, failed/interrupted turns, and empty `final_response` (D8, line 114), each with a test asserting the signal. Timeouts are centralized config keys rather than scattered defaults (D7), `usage` absent is `None` never `0` (D6), and the install hint is defined once (line 139). This satisfies the "no silent fallback values" project rule on the turn path.

findings.title: New auth-command I/O paths lack failure modes, a timeout, and the shared install hint
findings.description: The Login data flow goes straight from `login.login(mode)` to `AsyncCodex(config)` — it never calls `resolve_codex_runtime()`, and the "extra missing" row of the failure table is scoped to `create_agent` only (line 122). Yet the success criterion says "**any** `openai-oauth` use exits with an error containing the exact install command" (line 190), and Verification step 1 exercises only `review`/`model list`/`doctor` without the extra. Requirement left unmet: `sq auth login/logout/status` on a default install would hit a raw `ImportError` instead of the one shared hint string (line 139). Related gaps on these same new paths: `AsyncCodex.logout()` spawns a runtime (line 82) but D7 defines no timeout for it and no failure-table row covers SDK error, hang, transport close, or a partially completed logout; `webbrowser.open` failing or returning False on a headless box has no stated strategy ("attempt `webbrowser.open`"); and `login_chatgpt()` raising before a handle exists means the only specified cleanup — `handle.cancel()` on timeout/Ctrl-C (line 110) — cannot run. Add rows for login startup, pre-handle failure, browser-open failure and logout (including a bounded runtime-start + RPC timeout), and route all three commands through the shared resolver/hint.

findings.title: Doctor/model-list missing-extra handling is left implicit at a raising boundary
findings.description: D9 builds both consumers on `resolve_codex_runtime()`, which the Data Flow (line 80) says **raises** `ProviderError` when the package or binary is missing. But `ExtraRequirement.missing_extra_hint()` must return `str | None`, and the doctor check must return a `CheckResult` WARN row (Verification step 1, line 212) — neither contract permits a raised `ProviderError`. The design says "Doctor contains no import probing or `shutil.which` of its own" without stating which layer catches the resolver's error and converts it into the hint/detail, or how the row's `detail` (package version, runtime source) is produced when resolution fails. Slice 905's doctor contract requires the pure-check module to wrap unexpected exceptions in a typed, WARNING-logged handler that still emits a row; slice 381 restates that `run_all_checks` makes no subprocess call. Requirement left unmet: "sq doctor and sq model list run cleanly with and without the extra" (line 205). Specify the non-raising wrapper (and its single hint source) explicitly, plus a failure row and test for the wrapped exception.

findings.title: Parent's SDK startup NFR is not restated with a target; the 30 s status budget is unjustified
findings.description: The HLD's "System Architecture / SDK Agent Provider" and "SDK Agent Design Considerations" state a startup-cost constraint for SDK-subprocess providers (20–30 s CLI initialization; design for warm-pool/instance reuse rather than per-message creation), and the slice plan's Notes record 2–12 s+ per `query()`. This slice adds three new fresh-spawn command paths (login, logout, status) and explicitly declines any target: "No latency target is set" (line 82); no measured startup bound or reuse decision is given for them. More concretely, `codex.account_timeout_s = 30` (D7, line 109) covers "runtime start + `account()`", so a startup at the parent's stated 20–30 s leaves little or no room for the RPC — and the design's own failure row (line 126) then degrades to a WARNING row with **no account details**. That leaves the success criterion "sq auth status shows email and plan for a logged-in `openai-oauth`" (line 192) unmet on an in-spec slow startup. Restate the startup NFR with its numeric bound (or a measured Codex bound), and either split startup from the account RPC budget or raise/justify the cap so a normal startup cannot consume it.

findings.title: Several mechanisms are heavier than this slice needs
findings.description: Frontmatter says no planned slice consumes `InteractiveLogin`, `ExtraRequirement` or `CodexRuntime`, so the "Provides to Other Slices" generalizations are speculative. `ExtraRequirement` is a new `runtime_checkable` Protocol in `providers/base.py` with exactly one implementer, layered on top of the hint string that is already centralized in `runtime.py` and consumed by doctor/model list (line 139) — two mechanisms for one signal where the provider-side hint plus the shared resolver already satisfies "no profile-name check". `sq auth login --timeout SECONDS` (line 148) adds a second knob for a value D7 already centralizes in `codex.login_timeout_s`; the plan entry asks only for browser login and `--device-code`. Implementation step 0 (line 224) gates all of Part A on a live `OPENAI_API_KEY` fallback probe with a branching outcome that edits `OAuthFileStrategy` for a case the plan never assigns to slice 129. Cut/defer candidates: keep one hint mechanism (the shared `runtime.py`/provider hint) instead of a base-layer Protocol for one implementer; drop `--timeout` and use the config key; move the API-key fallback verification to its own bug-fix slice rather than making it a precondition of the port. This is trimming mechanisms, not dropping plan scope — Parts A/B/C remain intact.
